definitions.explanation: Finely chopped or sliced green onions used as a garnish or topping on Japanese dishes such as ramen, udon, miso soup, and tofu.

examples.japanese: ラーメンに{刻|きざ}み{葱|ねぎ}をのせる。
examples.english: To put chopped green onions on ramen.

examples.japanese: {刻|きざ}み{葱|ねぎ}をたっぷり{入|い}れてください。
examples.english: Please add plenty of chopped green onions.

examples.japanese: {冷奴|ひややっこ}の{上|うえ}に{刻|きざ}み{葱|ねぎ}と{生姜|しょうが}をのせて{食|た}べる。
examples.english: I eat cold tofu with chopped green onions and ginger on top.

notes:
One of the most common garnishes ({薬味|やくみ}) in Japanese cooking. {刻|きざ}む means 'to chop finely,' so {刻|きざ}み{葱|ねぎ} literally means 'chopped green onion.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- Topping for ramen, udon, soba, and {味噌汁|みそしる}
- Garnish on {冷奴|ひややっこ} (cold tofu) and {納豆|なっとう}
- Added to {焼|や}き{鳥|とり} and {丼物|どんぶりもの} (rice bowl dishes)

TYPES OF {葱|ねぎ}:
Usually made from the green part of {長葱|ながねぎ} (Japanese long onion) or {万能葱|ばんのうねぎ} (thin scallions). Sold pre-chopped at convenience stores and supermarkets.

OTHER COMMON {薬味|やくみ}:
- {生姜|しょうが}: ginger
- {大葉|おおば}: shiso leaf
- {鰹節|かつおぶし}: bonito flakes
- {七味|しちみ}{唐辛子|とうがらし}: seven-spice chili powder
